stories.headline: Binance says fake job interviews used as part of 6.3 billion dollars crypto hack
stories.script: Our lead story today. Hackers who stole a record 6.3 billion dollars (£4.7bn) from Binance used fake job interviews and a compromised internal AI tool, the firm has revealed. Initial findings published by the company, which operates the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said hackers gained access to its systems through "sophisticated, multi-stage campaign". It said they used a range of techniques such as malicious software downloads to compromise the computers of Binance engineers and gain control over tools to drain its wallet of billions of dollars worth of crypto. Binance called it a "serious and highly sophisticated security incident" and apologised, saying "this should not have happened".

stories.headline: AI inference chipmaker Moffett AI raises nearly RMB 1 billion in Series C+ funding
stories.script: In China. Moffett AI, a Shenzhen-based developer of AI inference chips, announced on November 3 that it had completed nearly RMB 1 billion in Series C+ funding. The financing follows another round of nearly RMB 1 billion approximately five months earlier. The proceeds will support upgrades to its sparse-computing inference chips, research into next-generation processors, and collaboration with research institutions and industry partners. Sparse computing reduces the calculations required to run AI models by exploiting sparsity in their data and operations. Moffett AI said it has deployed inference clusters across four regions in China and partnered with telecommunications operators. Its next-generation SP200 accelerator card is scheduled to arrive before the end of the year.

stories.headline: AI-powered malware ‘highly likely’ to be used to hack UK infrastructure by 2028
stories.script: Around the world. National Cyber Security Centre expects attacks on critical facilities such as power stations, airports and hospitals AI-powered malicious software is “highly likely” to be used in hacking attacks against the UK’s power stations, airports and hospitals by 2028, according to the state cybersecurity body. The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) said AI will probably enable a ransomware attack against critical national infrastructure [CNI] between now and 2028. The UK’s definition of CNI covers a range of facilities and services across sectors including energy, transport, defence, food, health and finance.

stories.script: In other news. Exclusive: Nonexistent precedent cited in alleged child rape case adds to dozens of AI-related errors plaguing court proceedings A senior crown prosecutor acting in a high court case cited an imaginary legal precedent in an error that has sparked fresh concerns about AI hallucinations infecting the justice system. Ravinder Dhillon, representing the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), referenced an entirely made-up case during a dispute over whether a child should be prosecuted for the rape of his younger sister, court documents have revealed.
